overview.headline: Branches of government roles and checks and balances

keyPoints.point: The Constitution divides federal government power into legislative, judicial, and executive branches.
keyPoints.quote: The Constitution of the United States divides the federal government into three branches:

keyPoints.point: The legislative branch is made up of Congress with Senate and House support offices.
keyPoints.quote: The legislative branch is made up of Congress:

keyPoints.point: Judicial work includes Interpreting the meaning of laws and deciding if laws violate the Constitution.
The president can veto legislation created by Congress as part of checks and balances.
keyPoints.quote: The president can veto legislation created by Congress.

keyTerms.gloss: elected body that makes up the legislative branch
keyTerms.quote: The legislative branch is made up of Congress:

keyTerms.gloss: highest federal court that evaluates laws for constitutionality
keyTerms.quote: The judicial branch includes the Supreme Court and other federal courts.

keyTerms.gloss: presidential rejection of legislation created by Congress
keyTerms.quote: The president can veto legislation created by Congress.

keyTerms.gloss: group of advisors to the president including department heads
keyTerms.quote: The cabinet members serve as advisors to the president.

keyTerms.gloss: system where each branch can respond to actions of other branches
keyTerms.quote: The ability of each branch to respond to the actions of the other branches is the system of checks and balances.

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains legislative, judicial, and executive branches, their members and key roles, and how checks and balances let each limit the others.
